hook: The Ancient "Underwater" Solution For Incredible Gut Health & Digestive Wellness
claim: VivoGut is marketed as a '14-in-1 gut health essential formula' that promotes smooth digestion, nutrient absorption and long-lasting gut balance. The 'underwater' theme refers to its seaweed ingredients.
ing_note: The page says there are 14 ingredients but only names these. Notably, this list (seaweed iodine, L-tyrosine, selenium and copper) is the classic make-up of a thyroid-support formula rather than a digestive one: it contains no fiber, no probiotics and no digestive enzymes.
use: The sales page does not state the daily dose in text; follow the label.
refund_note: To get a refund you must ship the bottles back to the fulfilment address in Aurora, Colorado, at your own cost.
bonuses: A guide to natural remedies for reflux
An immune and detox protocol guide
checks: None of the named ingredients has good clinical evidence for improving digestion or gut balance.
Kelp and bladderwrack add iodine, which is useful only if you are low and potentially harmful for people with thyroid disease.
L-tyrosine is described as 'boosting dopamine to encourage bowel movement'; there is no research supporting that claim.
Testimonials on the page are not verifiable and the seller states results 'will vary'.
cons: Ingredient list looks like a thyroid formula, not a gut formula
Only 9 of the claimed 14 ingredients are named, with no amounts
Iodine content is a concern for thyroid patients
Refunds require returning bottles at your own cost
verdict: VivoGut's ingredient list doesn't match its gut-health promise: it is mostly iodine-rich seaweed, minerals and an amino acid used to make thyroid hormone. People with digestive complaints are likely to get more from fiber, a studied probiotic or a doctor's check-up. Anyone with a thyroid condition should avoid it unless their doctor approves.
